main_text.p: non sit extra culpam, qui bonorum invasorem occidit, nisi etiam vitæ adsit periculum. Respondeo. 2. Etiam in hoc canone non eximitur homicida ab omni culpâ, cum illi ratione delicti commissi canonica pœna imponatur, puta ut jejunet, eleemosynas faciat. Neque obstat 2. Illud Innocentii 4. Qui ita: Præterea cum omnes leges, omniaque jura vim vi repellere, cunctisque sese defensare permittant: licuit utique ipsi Decano, (si prædictus Ballivus eum bonis suis mundanis injuriose spoliare, vel ea violenter occupare præsumpserit ut superius est expressum) contra illius violentiam, injuriamque se tueri. Respondeo enim 1. Non per allegatum canonem probatur, quod erat in quæ-stione, licere propter solam bonorum defensionem quem occidere, verum tantum innuitur, licitè quem suam pof-[?]e.dilecto.de sent.Excomm. in 6.

page.notes: The printed word "permittant" has a dark ink blot over its first letter, so the p is uncertain. The word "pof-" at the line end is hard to read and may be "pos-" or "poss-"; the catchword "sef." suggests the word continues on the next page. The left-margin notes are shown as three separate notes, aligned to the lines "Innocentii 4." and "Excomm. in 6.". Greek and Hebrew: none on this page.
